title: The premise that the subtraction needs
question: When may we call the difference a loss of energy of motion?
recap: The kinetic interpretation assumes that the additive energy offset is unchanged during emission.
premises: For each body state, H − E equals K plus an additive offset.
The same offset C applies before and after emission.
limitations: Without the unchanged-offset premise, the kinetic-energy drop is underdetermined.

overview.text: The traveler’s account contains the rest account plus energy of motion and an offset. The paper asserts that this offset does not change during emission. Only with that premise can the subtraction isolate the change in energy of motion.

full.spoken: Each frame-energy difference equals the corresponding kinetic energy plus the same additive constant C.

full.text: Because the same C occurs twice, it cancels. The kinetic-energy drop is then L(γ − 1), even though the body’s speed is unchanged. The unchanged offset is an asserted premise of this route, not something the subtraction independently measured.

full.spoken: The kinetic energy before minus the kinetic energy after equals L times gamma minus one.

full.returnCaption: Return to energy of motion at the same speed.

items: Let K₀ and K₁ be the body’s energy of motion, its kinetic energy, in the moving frame before and after the emission. In its rest frame the body does not move, so there it has none.
The premise: the difference between the two accounts is the kinetic energy plus a constant C that does not change when the body emits light. The same C before and after:

steps.spoken: Each frame-energy difference equals the corresponding kinetic energy plus the same additive constant C.

items: Subtract the second relation from the first: (H₀ − E₀) − (H₁ − E₁) = (K₀ + C) − (K₁ + C).
On the right, +C and −C cancel: K₀ + C − K₁ − C = K₀ − K₁.
The left side is the subtraction already worked out, L(γ − 1). So the kinetic-energy drop is:

steps.spoken: The kinetic energy before minus the kinetic energy after equals L times gamma minus one.

items: If the offsets were allowed to differ, C₀ before and C₁ after, the same steps would give (K₀ − K₁) + (C₀ − C₁) = L(γ − 1), and the kinetic-energy drop could not be separated from the change in offset. The unchanged C is what makes the identification possible, and it is asserted by this route, not measured.
The body moves at the same speed before and after, yet its kinetic energy drops. The small-speed passage compares this drop with Newton’s kinetic energy to find what changed.

steps.returnCaption: Return to energy of motion at the same speed.

margin.text: This is a productive conditional argument, not a premise-free theorem about arbitrary interacting extended systems. The paper’s comparison with the electron kinetic energy from relativity §10 is a comparison, not an additional premise used here.
